How to line a tote bag and turn it through the gap

How a lining goes in: one seam round the top, then the whole bag turns out through an opening in the lining. Shown on the tote and on the fabric basket, with two ways to close the opening.

Some links on this page are affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

Overview

The lined bag

The outer and the lining are sewn together round the top, turned through an opening in the lining and topstitched. Tap the bag to take it apart.

  2. 2Lining — sewn like the outer, kept inside out, then turned and pushed inside
  3. 3Opening — in a seam of the lining: 8 cm (3⅛ in) in a side seam on the tote, 15 cm (5⅞ in) in a corner seam on the basket · stitched closed at the edge
  4. 4Top seam — the outer and the lining right sides together, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Sew the lining the same way as the outer, and keep it inside out.

    In one side seam, leave an opening: on the tote it is 8 cm (3⅛ in), low down, just above the bottom.

    The opening can be any length, as long as the bag comes through it. A stiff item needs more room: the fabric basket, with its interfaced walls, has a 15 cm (5⅞ in) opening in a corner seam.

    Machine: straight stitch

  2. Turn the outer right side out; the lining stays inside out.

    On the tote, pin the straps to the top edge of the outer first: ends level with the edge, 6 cm (2⅜ in) from the centre, the loops hanging down over the bag.

    Slip the outer into the lining, so the right sides face each other and the straps are caught in between. Line up the side seams and the top edges, and clip them.

  3. Sew all the way round the top, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, through every layer: the lining, the straps and the outer.

    The tote and the basket both have a 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) seam here.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Reach into the opening in the lining, take hold of the outer and pull the whole bag out through it.

    Smooth the outer out: it is now right side out. The lining is right side out too and sticks out above the bag, its opening still open.

  5. Tuck the raw edges of the opening inside, in line with the rest of the seam, so that the two folds meet.

    The first way, on the machine: stitch the two folds together at the very edge. This is how the tote and the basket are closed; the seam then goes inside the bag, out of sight.

    The second way, by hand, with a ladder stitch (also called a slip stitch): press the two folds, thread a needle with thread that matches the fabric and hide the knot inside one fold.

    Take a small stitch inside one fold, then go straight across and take a small stitch inside the other one. Keep going from side to side: the threads between the folds look like the rungs of a ladder.

    Every few stitches, pull the thread: the edges close and the stitches disappear. At the end, secure the thread and hide its end inside the lining.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Push the lining down inside the outer, right to the bottom.

    On the tote, press the top edge flat with the iron. On the basket, smooth the lining into the corners.

  7. Topstitch all the way round the top, through the outer and the lining: 1 cm (⅜ in) from the edge on the tote, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) on the basket.

    Your bag is done!

    Machine: straight stitch

What you'll need

Thread, sewing clips, thread snips, an iron and the sewing machine — the tools I personally recommend for these steps. To close the opening by hand you will also need a hand-sewing needle.
